# PackMan v1.9.2 — Windows reliability and performance

This Windows-only point release builds on the Windows 1.9 series. The previously published Windows 1.9.1 and macOS 1.10 releases remain available. WSL2 is planned separately.

## What's improved on Windows

- Search by package name, package ID, source, repository or status. The toolbar shows visible and total selections; select/deselect visible rows independently of all updates. **Update Selected** still processes every checked update, including checked rows hidden by a search.
- Scan results are invalidated when a source is enabled, disabled or reconfigured. Failed source retries no longer leave outdated executable contexts available for installation. Package details use one Activity window, and obsolete package actions cannot start an installer.
- Scoop, npm, pip, pipx and Chocolatey distinguish malformed or unsuccessful scans from recognised empty results. Valid partial results remain visible with their source issue.
- New ignore rules distinguish WinGet repositories. Existing 1.9 ignore rules retain their original scope; remove and recreate a legacy rule if you want it limited to a particular repository.
- Package-manager installation is offered only for a confirmed missing manager or an explicit missing prerequisite. Configured but broken tools instead show recovery guidance.
- History is written in batches before and after update runs, while individual running/installation checkpoints remain durable. Writes run away from the UI thread, and history rows are refreshed incrementally. Command-log delivery and bulk selection are more responsive.
- Tool-probe caches expire and are invalidated by executable or PATH changes. pipx capabilities are checked again when the executable or reported version changes.
- Python and NuGet version ordering now accounts for their respective version conventions; WinGet verifies unambiguous numeric revisions without assuming all versions are SemVer.
- pipx's legacy fallback checks a plain package in its own configured environment and reports custom or constrained environments as requiring review. .NET tool discovery avoids substituting nuget.org for an unfamiliar/private configured feed; it offers public-feed candidates only when nuget.org is the sole confirmed enabled feed and the installed version is present there.
- A successful manual PackMan update check clears an obsolete update banner; a failed network check retains the prior information.
- The updater finds the newest stable release with Windows assets, even if a newer Mac-only tag exists.

## Performance

In local synthetic tests of 100 successful updates, history saves decreased from 400 to 202 and history-writing time fell by about 54–55%, while keeping recovery checkpoints. Real-world performance will vary.

## Downloads

- **PackMan-Windows-x64.exe** — standalone Windows executable.
- **PackMan-Windows-x64.zip** — ZIP package; extract and run PackMan.exe.
- Both downloads include SHA-256 checksum files.

For macOS, use [PackMan 1.10](https://github.com/dklasens/PackMan/releases/tag/v1.10).

## Requirements

Windows 10/11 x64 and the .NET 10 Desktop Runtime, as in 1.9. Existing settings and update history are retained. Old tool-probe caches are refreshed automatically as part of the settings schema update.

## Testing

The Windows implementation was built and tested against .NET 10. See the [implementation and validation record](https://github.com/dklasens/PackMan/blob/v1.9.2/IMPLEMENTATION_1.9.1.md) for details.
